utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Re: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vukovic. Mr. Vukovic, while you still have the extracts of the report in front of you, I just want to ask you about two others to try and give the Trial Chamber some representative spread and sample of the buildings that you inspected in December 1991. Could you please turn to X-5, which is 10-5. It's for the record 01069612 with photographs appended, 9613 and 9614, and the English is 01069612. It's a building described as the Katic - that's with a "K" - palace at 2 Gunduliceva Poljana. Firstly, Mr. Vukovic, are you familiar with this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall inspecting that building with Mrs. Peko and Mr. Vetma on -- as described there, the 10th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The remarks at the bottom of the assessment -- underneath "assessment" say: "The building has been visited by somebody and rubble has been cleared. The keys are to be found with the Dragicevic family. Inside the building, a collection of portable historical monuments has been recorded." Where did you obtain that information from?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We obtained this information from the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get access to the building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After having inspected the neighbour's apartment, because this block has several entrances, after receiving this information, we got the keys from the Dragicevic family. These people happened to be neighbours of my mother, too, in Dubrovnik. So that is what made it easier to get the keys and also to speak to them generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just briefly describe the type of building this is to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a typical building, a very high-class building in terms of Dubrovnik architecture. It is a very valuable building because it's interiors are very well preserved from the Baroque period. In a way, it is a paradigmatic example of a Dubrovnik townhouse, and its interior could still be seen in the original form. That would be it very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The description of the damage refers to "a direct hit to the east side of the roof close to the apex above the staircase and through the transom light." What was the information you received or the inspection you made which enabled you to record the details of a direct hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember as I read this text. I'm trying to remember this specific building. There is reference to the stairwell and the area above it, and that made it obvious that there was that kind of damage involved. So we simply recorded the damage as it is recorded here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say now how you were able to record that the date of the hit was the 6th of December 1991? What was the information which enabled you to record the date of the hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this information followed our previous experience. We spoke to the actual tenants or the neighbours. So that was our primary source of information. We had another level of information, the actual traces of impact. This building had to be marked in view of its historical importance, and what I said a few moments ago, what a valuable monument it was. So that shows its relevance within the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please just look at the photographs, that's 01069613 and 9614. Are those photographs of the Katic palace and do they depict the damage to the roof and building that you've described in your report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is certainly the building. And what is shown here is exactly what we talked about. Actually, it is the block in front of the rector's palace, and it is very impressive and memorable. So one has to recognise it even in these photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the information contained on this report form, it's 01609612, accurate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have to intervene. I have my own version. I imagine that these codes that you refer to just now have to do with the paper I have before me. So could we please check this before I actually make a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document you should have in front of you has a number on the top right-hand corner, 01069612. It's the Prosecutor's evidence number. And that is on the page with the building number X-5, 10-5.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you haven't understood my point. I only have my very own copy here, not the copy that I had yesterday, the one that the Court provided me with yesterday. So if I could have that, please. It is the same document, so I can give you an answer. This statement here is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to clarify, the numbers of the photographs that you were looking at before, are they 01069613 and 01069614? Two photographs referred to a moment ago, from your own identical copy of the document before the Court.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at the description and the authors -- or the people who inspected it, that's you, that's yourself, Mr. Vetma, and Mrs. Peko. Could you remember now what each of you did in that particular inspection?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said already, or rather I said yesterday, that we toured the area together, made notes, and commented on everything that we saw. So we defined all of this together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a general practice. My question is just in relation to this building, can you remember now all these years later specifically what each of the three of you did when you inspected the Katic palace together?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not remember the details. It's been quite a while, hasn't it? So I can't really answer your question with any degree of precision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The last one I want to take you to is number XI-29, which is the record 01069680. The translation is L0061526, described as 9 Od Domina Street, the house of Kukuljica. Firstly, are you familiar with that particular building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd need to look at the map. I need to jog my memory after all because I think this is a smallish building, and I don't seem to remember it very well. But if you allow me, if I look at the map, then I may give a more specific answer. It's a smallish building, as I said. It's at the intersection of two streets, Od Domina and Strossmayerova. Yes, this is one of the many buildings that had to be identified on the basis of this additional insight. I do remember the building now, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The details record you as having inspected it on the 16th of December at 13.50 hours and describe the damage as ricocheting shrapnel causing minor damage to the roof cover, blast impaired static stability. You said it's the house of Kukuljica. How did you get the information as to the date of the hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same situation. Quite simply, neighbours provided information, and I think that what you said just now has to do with that type of identification. It practically had a decisive role in terms of identifying the time and date of impact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building I showed you before, the Katic palace, that's X-5, had some photographs attached. Do you know whether this one, XI-29, 9 Od Domina Street, whether any photographs were taken of this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just take a look in my own documents here. I think there aren't any. Perhaps some could be found elsewhere, but I would not be in a position to identify them now. And there aren't any here as identified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there aren't any there as identified in the report, why wouldn't there be photographs of this particular building attached to the report whereas there are photographs of other buildings that we went through today and yesterday, such as the cathedral, the Katic palace, Miha Pracata 6, and so on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it had to do with a principle of accessibility as far as photography is concerned. You know yourself that when buildings are so densely built, then it is hard to find the right angle to take a picture. Perhaps it is included in one of the panoramic pictures, but now why they were not here, I cannot say. But it was not of such decisive importance for what we had elaborated here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The form shows -- records you and Mr. -- sorry, records the inspection being done by you and Mr. Davorka -- sorry, Davorka Kunic. Are the details of your inspection accurately recorded in this report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It was recorded. How should I put this? In our first review, we managed to establish whether there was more or less damage sustained. This is a building that was put in the category of those with the least degree of damage. So the only thing we said was that this building had been damaged, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it about the details or your inspection there which enables you to put it in the category of least damage, that is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it has to do with an indirect hit and the effects of that indirect hit, that is to say, shrapnel that ricocheted from the point of direct impact. This showed a lesser degree of damage, and it could be readily discerned. So we did not need to check and verify and analyse it to any major extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've taken you to, I think, eight or nine separate buildings out of the 55 listed in the index to the buildings bearing your name as one of the inspectors in the report. Have you reviewed each of the buildings or the details of the inspection of each of the buildings listed in that index which is attached to the extracts containing the reports of the buildings you inspected?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it has to do with the material that I obtained yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's an identical copy of the -- of all the buildings in the folder you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I. The Defence would like to know what this document is, the document that the distinguished witness is looking at here. As far as I can see from this side, it is not what was distributed to everyone in the courtroom, the Trial Chamber and everybody else. The second question is who gave him this and what is it? Because he started his evidence yesterday, so we need to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can deal with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, can you just confine -- you've brought some of your own material based on the report, I understand, with you. I just want you to confine yourself to the folder which you were provided with in Court yesterday. That's the one you have been looking at this morning. So just close your bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That probably arose because at the beginning the witness didn't have the Court copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was my fault. I assumed when I saw him with one in front that it was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And while the witness is looking, I'm told on reliable authority that the number in the folder is 63, not 55, separate buildings. You took the witness to three more than you identified in your evidence, just to show you that one of us at least is awake.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And keeping reliable and accurate statistics, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Vukovic, if you're going to flick through every page, you could possibly do that during the break, and I'll move on to something else at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If that's acceptable to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness might mark somehow the point he has reached to save him more time, and you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness... Can the witness please be provided with a copy of P51/ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've got a copy in front of you, a document which we have been referring to as the Institute Preliminary Report. What was the purpose, the main purpose, of this report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary purpose of this report was to see what the situation was on all buildings that had been damaged at the time and to establish a technical component, if I can put it that way, which would be used for an overall assessment of the intervention that was necessary. It is called "preliminary" precisely for that reason, that it had to be analysed further, which would ultimately lead to establishing the actual damage and the amounts that were required for the repair. Also, it needed to be established whether the premises could still be used for housing. So those would be the basic components, if I can put it that way, that were the motive for this preliminary inspection, or rather preliminary report. And as I said, that was the only purpose. We had no idea where this would end up and what else it would be used for. So this is material that in our estimate is a faithful picture of the situation as it was during our inspection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you had no idea where it would end up and what else it would be used for. When it was prepared, was it prepared with litigation in mind?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, and I think at that time as far as I know it wasn't something that we envisaged in view of the things that we were dealing with at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an estimate of the cost of repair made as a result of that report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't personally work on that. I've already said that in my testimony yesterday. This was done by experts from an institution which was to take over the operative part of the reconstruction and which was established after the earthquake in 1979 in Dubrovnik. It was called the Dubrovnik Reconstruction Office. And based on our information which we made in our preliminary report, and a methodology which as far as I can recall was based on the degree of damage and the footage of the space, the price of the damage, direct damage, was formed. This was the immediate direct damage. And as far as I can remember from conversations with my colleagues, because I didn't participate, in this in the first draft, based on the preliminary reports, it amounted to 17.5 million dollars. But this was not the final sum in view of the fact that there were some additional information which was based on the fact that the buildings were already a little unstable because of the earthquake. So that due to the detonations from the shelling, the degree of damage from before, from 1979, on these buildings involving cracks and some constructional damage -- structural damage which affected the technical state of the building and brought its usage safety a little bit down. The additional damage was estimated at 4 million dollars, and this information was also obtained, and I'm speaking about information that I gleaned from conversations. I don't have any information, official information about this. But this is the amount of the damage established at the time and which at the time was probably the subject of conversations about how and in what way to approach the reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned the estimate being based upon a footage of space. Do you mean by that a square -- a cost per square -- a figure per square metre of damage depending upon what was actually damaged in the structure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time it served as the quickest way to get to the value of the damage. So we're talking about the square metres of the space.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have recorded with some precision in some of your reports of damage an area measured in square metres of damage to, for example, a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. roof. Was it because of the need to estimate the cost of repairs based upon square metres of damage that you did it, or was it for some other reason, or was it a combination of reasons?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main reason was to describe more closely what could be seen of the damage. So it served to illustrate what we actually wrote relating to specific buildings. But whether it was used for some additional purposes, for example, to assess exactly how many square metres of different construction materials you needed, for example, timber and things like that, this was perhaps then used as a kind of secondary information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any one person responsible for the compilation or the collation of the entire report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsibility was to the extent that somebody on behalf of the institution needed to sign the whole thing. I don't know if there is such a signature or not on the complete report which numbers a number of volumes. But in any case, the responsibility rested with the people who were coordinating the entire project and on the people who participated in this identification itself. So there should have been a kind of order for the responsibility for everything that is stated in the reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By my last question, I meant administrative responsibility. Did anyone have overall administrative responsibility for the physical compilation, or collation of all the reports, the typing up and putting them into report form?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A report as a kind of summary, I don't know if that form of report exists, and I don't know if anybody signed such a report. What I was talking about is all of this material that I know that exists, and that's these volumes of the report. So that is all that I can say on that matter at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just turn to the introduction to the report. In the English, it's at page L0061414. It's 01069061 in the B/C/S. It's signed by Dorotea Valjalo, lawyer. Was she the director of the institute at the time? And it's dated the 6th of January 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Miss Dorotea Valjalo is a lawyer in the department for the preservation of historical or cultural monuments. And at the time, she was the director of the institute. So she was the administrative authority about which you wanted to know, I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the information contained in that introduction accurate and reliable -- or accurate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to read. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the information accurate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go back to -- go back one or two pages. That's to the credit page so to speak, 01069058, which lists the task team of the people involved in the compilation of the report. It should be the third page from the front.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this book, unless it's in the first book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just have access to that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Not the third, but a little bit further on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under task team, it describes authors as Matko Vetma, Zvonimir Franic, Bozena Popovic, and Slobodan Vukovic. Firstly, there's an error in the English translation, draft translation at L0061412. The name of Bozena Popovic, which is written in English. The name should be Popic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underneath the authors are the consultants, Bruno Karneze and Colin Kaiser of UNESCO, followed by collaborating members Lucijana Peko and a number of other people, underneath which are technical members in collaborating institutions. The four authors -- Mr. Vetma, what was his role or job at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Matko Vetma is an architect. And at the time, he gave a kind of architectural interpretation of the information reaching the institute. And in a way, he was able to present everything to be able to get a relevant technical set of data about what was being done on these cultural monuments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the person who contacted or coordinated or liaised with the UNESCO people, that's Dr. Kaiser and Mr. Karneze?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Matko Vetma, who speaks French and English and Italian, directly contacted with Mr. Karneze and Dr. Kaiser, and of course with all the other colleagues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one is Zvonimir Franic. What was Zvonimir Franic's role in this project and who is he?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's also an architect, a colleague, a younger colleague, who also worked on the technical aspects of the preservation of cultural monuments and in the interpretation of certain data that we were receiving. And he also participated in the final drafting of the final material in the graphic sense, first of all, and let's say in a system of processing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Professor Bozena Popic and what was her role?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She's also employed in the Institute for the preservation of cultural monuments and she was in charge of the moveable heritage or paintings and everything that in a way is connected with buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she have a role in recording the moveable heritage in the Old Town and any damage to it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was her primary function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're the fourth author described there. What was the difference between an author and a consultant for the purposes of this report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author of that, and we will give it a kind of working title, and it's something that's a little bit unusual, to use that term "author." What we wanted to stress is there was a kind of core of experts which created first of all an atmosphere of enthusiasm and which kept up this atmosphere throughout the whole time. This is an undisputable fact, and I was very proud because of this. At the time, and I must say that this authorship in a way implies first of all the team which perhaps in a different context should have been the heart and the brain of that whole project.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underneath consultants, consulting members, including people who are listed as having inspected buildings with you such as Lucijana Peko and Davorka Kunic. Some of those people are architects; some are described as architectural technicians. What was the difference between an author, or the role of an author and that of the collaborating members who are listed there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The collaborating members were a kind of physical, technical assistants. They were supposed to speed up the whole procedure of identification since there were not enough people at the time at the Institute for the Preservation of Cultural Monuments because this quantity of buildings was supposed to be registered as quickly as possible. So we asked our colleagues in urban planning, and I'm thinking of Ms. Davorka Kunic first of all, Ms. Anka Buzic, Ms. Mirjana Karaman, and Mr. Zeljko Franetovic who together with me on my initiative after I spoke with my colleague Matko Vetma by telephone joined the team which was to go out on this inspection. So their function was technical so that this large number of facilities could be covered as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the role of the technical members described -- who are listed underneath collaborating members, that's Milenko Mojas, the photographer you told the Trial Chamber about yesterday, the other photographer, a graduate economist, a graduate engineer, and a typist? What was their role in this project?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical collaborators were Milenko Mojas who was a technical photographer at the Institute for the Preservation of Cultural Monuments. Bozidar Djukic was also a professional photographer, but he's a journalist, a photo journalist. And then we're talking about the typists. I personally don't know who these people are, but I assume that they are from the administrative part of the institute. And I had limited contacts with that sector, and I practically don't know who these people were. But I think that more or less this is the team that was in the institute's administrative sector at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Collaborating institutions which are listed below, the first one is the Institute for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection Dubrovnik. Was that the body or the office attached to the municipality for which you were working in 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an institution which was the only one that dealt with urban planning for the Dubrovnik Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you consulted by Ms. Valjalo before she wrote her introduction to this report, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the report completed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was in the beginning of January 1992. I don't know the exact date. But I think it was in the -- in early January. I remember that a press conference was organised in our large conference room. Journalists were present, TV crews. And I think this was, if I remember rightly, in early January 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the authors or other people involved in the project meet before the press conference to talk about the report and its contents and how to present it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no official meetings. These were mostly unofficial contacts. We were in daily contacts to a lesser or greater degree. And the usual team that is noted here as the authors, this team actually formed a concept of how to present our case or ourselves before the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you personally read the entire report or went through it before its publication and the press conference in early January 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in detail, in every paper. But I did go over most of it. Of course, I was interested in that -- in those parts where I was personally featured. As far as the other things are concerned, I just was curious to see how much material there was and how this was presented, how -- the way in which it was presented. And I must say that I was impressed with the manner in which such a quantity of material was presented in such a short period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say that on page 17, line 6, the witness said something that was not adequately interpreted. He said that he just went over this in a summary way, in a quick, fast way. He kind of glanced over the material. That is the gist what have the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. That flows on to what is recorded as not in detail. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having looked through the report in the detail which we've just mentioned and Mr. Petrovic has added to, how do you assess the report's reliability in terms of assessing -- sorry, identifying and assessing the damage to the Old Town as of early January 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said here that the material was used for the preliminary identification, meaning that the degree of processing and the level of damage assessment could have been more detailed than was presented here. So it's material which meets the lowest level of certainty regarding the material here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what about its reliability in meeting that lowest level of certainty? How would you describe the overall reliability of the information contained in the report that you've looked through?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a large percentage, up to about 95 per cent I would dare to say, the identification is reliable. And on the whole, I think that it satisfied our goals which we had at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to show -- excuse me. I wish to show the witness a clip, a portion of Exhibit P66, which is the video that Mr. Grbic provided. There's actually a transcript. I wish to start the clip. I'm going to show the witness a clip from, for the record, the time of 34.55 to 37 minutes. And from 37.38 to 37.53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Of what, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of the Exhibit P66, which is a video which Mr. Grbic produced. It's the compilation video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of you, Mr. Vukovic, you will see a portion of the video. I just want you to identify -- if you can identify anything, to point it out, just say "stop" and we will stop it and we will make a record and come back to it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So could the video be played, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just stop you there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is Stradun. It's the southern side of Stradun. I beg your pardon. Just a small correction. It's not the southern side; it's the northern side. I've noticed just now. This is where the Franciscan cloister is, so it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was at 35.05. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've stopped at 35.34. It shows a street and some people standing in a street. Which street is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is Od Puca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you say about the damage there relative to what you saw when you walked through Od Puca on the morning of the 7th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in front of a building that had burned down completely. I think it's the palace close to the street of Miha Pracata, a big building. I don't know if that will do for the time being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told the Trial Chamber that you walked through Od Puca on the morning of the 7th of December, and you saw damage and debris. How does the damage and debris which you can see in that video compare to that what you saw and described yesterday to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just a very short clip which is supposed to jog my memory. I can recall that this is what the pavement looked like with a lot of debris, glass shards. Quite simply, I mean it was difficult to pass through the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We just showed a building at 35.43. 35.43, do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a house in the street Od Puca. It's the palace that I mentioned a few minutes ago, the one that I said was close to Miha Pracata. It had burned down completely. And I have a lasting memory of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this one of the buildings you inspected?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the buildings I inspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 35.46 and 47, there's another building there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that St. Vlaho's church?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question that is being put by my learned friend is a leading question. I believe the witness will recognise it because anybody would. But I would just like my colleague to be careful and to bear this in mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that building, Mr. Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me about the damage we can see close up, that is the terrace in front of St. Blaise's church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 35.52, what's that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Stradun viewed from the west towards the bell tower. I think that on the left-hand side we see the ground floor of the festival building. That is where the main building of the Dubrovnik summer festival is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How does the debris on the pavement compare to what you saw on the 7th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a less striking example because we can see that the pavement has already been cleaned to a certain extent. So we do not see the full effect of the fire and everything else that led to the destruction of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can just look on the left-hand side of the picture, there's a fire hose which seems to be leading towards a door and you can see a wall. Do you know which particular building this is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question, this is the building that I described only a short while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There's a building, you can see a red hose going diagonally directly towards a door, and there's a window. I just want you to look at the wall. It's on the left-hand side of the screen. You can see some marks on the wall.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How clearly on the monitor in front of you can you see marks, pockmarks on the wall of that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the damage can be seen, primarily that caused by shrapnel. And I also think that the window posts and lintels were obviously destroyed, too, because of the extreme heat. That is to say that it was all turned into limestone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stopped at 35.58. I'm sure my learned friend won't mind me leading on this particular building. Is that the Onofrije fountain, Mr. Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Onofrije fountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop at 36.04. There's a street shown there. Which street is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Siroka Ulica, Siroka Street, viewed from Stradun facing the south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the debris shown there similar to the debris you described yesterday on your walk through that street, the Siroka Street, on the 7th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop at 36.08. There's a burnt-out building there. Do you know which building that is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the facade of the building that I mentioned a short while ago, the one that I said that remains in my lasting memory. It's in Od Puca. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 36.12, stop there. Is that the same building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same building. It is a fragment of this building that is closer to Miha Pracata Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop at 36.15. There's a narrow street there with a man walking down it. Which street is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a street near St. Joseph's church. So when you go down Od Puca, there are streets on the side, and I think there's a building on the left-hand side there that had burned down completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's St. Joseph's Street. This was the entrance into the palace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you mentioned entrance into the palace. Was that the same palace you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's the palace on the corner that's in the row of palaces that burned down in the same street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in St. Joseph's Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We just stopped at 36.19. Is that a building on the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He can say no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think the question has to be does the witness know what building this is, rather than leading him on, suggesting that it is this or that. I think that this is an unfair way of putting questions. I can understand his fervour, wanting to prove something that's extremely difficult, but please...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The fervour is just trying to move the proceedings on, but I won't lead if there's an objection to...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That seems to be the position, Mr. Re. So you're on notice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That building, do you know where that building is, Mr. Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on Stradun, and I know the building. It is the ground floor of a block which is on the corner of Siroka and Stradun. This is where a bookstore was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a building you inspected?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. But it was in the block that I worked on, too. I think it was number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you say about the marks on the walls near the windows -- near the window and underneath the window?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are actually marks of a fire. They show that there was shrapnel, too, that damaged the building, the facade. So when a shell would fall on Stradun, then this is the effect it would cause on the neighbouring buildings. So I think there were two important matters here: One is that the damage was due to shrapnel and to fire. The fire probably came from direct impact nearby or something like that. So that would be my present observation with regard to that particular case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 36.34 shows -- seems to show the top floor of a building. Do you know which building that one is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm assuming that this is Stradun. Another matter now. I think this is a building -- could I have a broader view of it, if possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We'll see what we can do. No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that this is a building that is near a building on Stradun, near the festival building, which is on Stradun. This is one of the upper floors. That's what it looks like. It's the profile that's suggested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the building at 36.34 on the video. We'll just keep on moving through. 36.38, which building is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the cathedral, the dome of the cathedral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next one, 36.42, do you know which building that one is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The festival building. Or rather, the Dubrovnik summer festival building. That is what it was called, and that is what it is called nowadays as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 36.50, do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It is St. Joseph's church in Od Puca Street. And the damage can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a building you inspected?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 36.54, do you recognise that street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not with any certainty. But I assume that it's one of the streets leading from Prijeko to Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've given you a wider view or a longer view. Does that assist, 36.59?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you say about the debris or the rubble on the ground which was near the man at about 56.56 -- sorry, 36.56?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please rewind it a bit so that I can see it somewhat better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's coming.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stop. Yes, I can say that that is approximately the situation that was there just after I first walked into town. That is to say, lots of rubble which made accessibility very difficult. That is the main characteristic. The material obviously fell off the roofs because damaged roof tiles can be seen here. And also some of the stone material that is hard for me to define on the basis of this footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just point out to the Trial Chamber where you can see in that photo damaged roof tiles?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how I can show this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it something that you --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here. Here is this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you tell us where it is, we can move the cursor around.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cursor is where it is. It's reddish-brown, yellowish, reddish, something like that. And then if you can go left with the cursor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The cursor was just to the right of the person wearing a beret standing in the middle of the photo at about his knee height. It has just been moved to the left --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. At the same level. Yes, these are bigger parts of the roof tiles, as far as I can see from this. It's not very precise, but it is very, very likely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you said a moment ago that this is a street that runs between Prijeko and the Stradun.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That completes that part. We'll move to 15 seconds between 37.38 and 37.53. The video shows some people on top of some roofs. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you exactly which building this is. But since I see in the background the dome of the Orthodox church, it is most probably block number 8, somewhere in block number 8. But I cannot say anything more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see any roof damage there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that block, I did not examine the damage. Not on this building specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see any damage in the video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It can be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you just point it out to the Trial Chamber where it is. There are two figures. Where is it relative to the two figures, one wearing a red shirt and the other one wearing a dark top?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The damage is under the feet of the man in the red sweater. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 37.35, what is that a view of?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a panoramic view from the city walls, from the western side above Pile gate. That is what can be seen close to us. It is a damaged wall. Then in the background, Pasko Milicevic Poljana can be seen. That is where the Onofrije fountain is, and also a building with a damaged roof can be seen. That is actually the first building on the corner of Stradun and Poljana Pasko Milicevica, which is a square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said there was a damaged wall. Is the damaged wall on the city walls itself?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it is part of the damaged wall which belongs to the city walls itself, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop. 37.38, what's that a view of?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is most probably a view from the same point but facing Minceta, so it's probably in the northern part of town. And the damage can be seen again on the parapet and parts of the stone material that fell off. This was probably a direct hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 37.45, there's a view with some smoke arising out of some buildings. What can you say about --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the festival building that was still surrounded by smoke. That can be seen because this is the bell tower of the Franciscan cloister. Near it is a building that burned down completely. So it is with a considerable degree of certainty that I can say that. Also what can be seen is fire, most probably on one of the buildings in Od Puca Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That completes that clip, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be a convenient time for the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the witness could, as discussed before, just review the -- for consistency the documents from the Court against those which he has to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That can occur during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, have you had a chance to look through the bundle of documents over the break?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that contain a copy of all the buildings you inspected in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are the extracts from the Institute Preliminary Report, P51/ID. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you satisfied as to the accuracy of the information recorded on each of the pages, inspection reports --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution intends to move to have the extracts tendered into evidence. I'm not quite sure of the statistics, but I think I showed him 10, 11, or 12 -- 10 buildings, 11 buildings. 11 buildings out of the 63. For the purposes of -- I understand my learned friend, Mr. Petrovic, from a discussion with him, he's objecting to the tendering of those portions of the report. How far --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps we might hear Mr. Petrovic, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence is opposed to having this extract of the document which is in front of the witness, to have it used -- to have it tendered into evidence. The reason why we feel this way is -- has already been expressed during our work on this case. I do not wish to take up your time, Your Honours, to repeat all of this. I just want to point out some aspects of the reasons why we are opposed to tendering this exhibit. I will start from the simplest of reasons, and you will understand why, Your Honours. The document that my learned colleague is trying to have admitted contains things that the witness does not work on. If you closely look at the document, there are some parts of it on which the witness did not work on at all. My learned colleague probably made a mistake because the translation was wrong, but for example if we look at location marked IX-25, we will see that this location was processed by Matko Vetma. This is also in this binder that has been tendered. This is just one example of numerous mistakes and numerous mistakes and problems that this document contains. We will deal with some of them in our cross-examination. But the number of inconsistencies, mistakes, incorrect facts is such that we feel that this document does not satisfy the minimum standards required for it to be adopted as an exhibit by the Trial Chamber. I'm not going to go into details. I will deal with that during our cross-examination. But in any case, we strongly object to this. The second set of reasons relates to the fact that only a few buildings were inspected, 11 or perhaps a few more, out of a total of 60-odd buildings. To the question from the Trial Chamber, the witness knew only about three buildings. Everything else is something that he has read out. And all of the rest is something that's not based on his recollection. So we simply do not have an adequate way of determining that the document that is being tendered is reliable enough and it is -- has -- contains enough probative value to be admitted. I am convinced, and I hope that the Trial Chamber will also be convinced, the Defence will certainly try to do this during the cross-examination of this witness, about what I have just said. And we believe that this document should not be admitted into evidence, but should just be given an ID number. I could go through this whole set of documents, but I'm afraid that that would take up too much time so I will not do that unless it's necessary, unless the Trial Chamber feels that the arguments I have put forward are insufficient in which case I am prepared to do that. In any case, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Re, concern is expressed in particular about building IX-25. There does appear to be a difference between the B/C/S and the English language of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. My learned friend is completely correct. Those were supposed to be removed from the binders before they were handed up. In a rush to get them done, it must have been omitted and shouldn't be in the index either. He is quite correct in relation to that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are there others of that nature?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: None that I know of. That's the only one that I know of that should have been removed. If Mr. Petrovic could point to others which he says shouldn't be there, which he says the witness didn't inspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you permit me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a whole series of other documents from this same binder which cannot be admitted into evidence, a whole series of them. And this will be the content of our cross-examination so that in any event we suggest that your decision on this matter be postponed until we have completed our cross-examination. And then we propose that the -- this document is not accepted into evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I take it, Mr. Re, you persist in your tender of all but the documents relating to IX-25.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct. I certainly do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Concern arises, the witness has apparently identified all the documents in here as his. Are we sure about his position on IX-25?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you might have reason to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, building number IX-25, in Croatian, that's 01069585, in the B/C/S it says it was inspected by Mr. Vetma. And in the English, L0059975, it said it was inspected by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an obvious mistake in the English translation. The information in the Croatian is correct, so I did not work on this building. I noticed this, but I did not include that in my interpretation, that it's identical. But I don't think that this changes anything substantially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're just concerned at the moment to ensure that there are no other buildings in the bundle you have there which you did not personally inspect. Apart from one, which has slipped through, were there any others?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look at the English version. I looked at the Croatian version, and I think what is in the Croatian version is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Apart from IX-25, were there any other buildings in that bundle that do not bear your name as having inspected them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I checked everything in the Croatian version, and that corresponds to what I worked on, whether alone or in a group.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you permit me to give you another brief argument, although the moment is not suitable to make this argument since this will be the subject of our cross-examination, so I apologise in advance to the Trial Chamber. 50 per cent or approximately 50 per cent of the reports before you, Your Honours, were compiled before the 13th of December 1991. Why do I mention the 13th of December, Your Honours? The same day that the witness signed the reports on the buildings that he allegedly inspected, on that same day, he also signed a statement to an investigator of the OTP that he began work, his work, on the 13th of December. So 50 per cent more or less of documents or reports contained in this binder were drafted before the 13th of December, and on the same day that he signed the reports that he did, he also signed a statement to an investigator stating that he has joined this work on the 13th of December. This is another one in a series of arguments that we intend to present during our cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that the tender, except for item IX-25, should be received at this stage. Could I indicate that the live question clearly is the reliability that is to be attached to the content, but on the face of the present evidence, the document is clearly relevant. It is clearly directly of probative value to issues which this Chamber must decide. And it is of a nature which on the present evidence indicates that it is the product, the work of the witness with others, and he vouches generally for its accuracy and reliability. Even so, of course, some of the content is based on what others have told the witness, neighbours or tenants and the like, and therefore, is subject to assessment as to weight by the Chamber in due course. And of course, the reliability and, therefore, the weight which the Chamber might place on this report may well be significantly affected during cross-examination. But at the time of tender, which is now, it appears to us that a sufficient basis has been laid to justify its receipt into evidence with the exception of the documents relating to IX-25. It will therefore be received as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May I also move into evidence at the same time the index.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's just get that one in. Stage by stage, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not too much further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked P174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Re, you want to admit something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is the index we have prepared to Exhibit P174. Of course, with the exception of number IX-25. We can, of course, during the break delete that particular entry from the index, if it would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Where is the entry to be found?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Page 3, the 7th item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was looking at the wrong document. My fault. The members of the Chamber are able to strike that out and have done so on page 3. But is it really an exhibit, or is it merely an aide memoire to the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's an aide memoire to the exhibit, Your Honour. Perhaps it should be appended to P174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As an index.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will do that. It will be received as part of P174. And there have been deleted from it on page 3 the reference to building IX-25. I got my tense wrong there. "There has been deleted..." Now, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, Mr. Petrovic just raised a matter relating to a statement which you gave to ICTY -- sorry, Office of the Prosecutor investigators on the 6th of July 2000. Do you have a copy of the statement there with you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have it in English and Croatian?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you just turn to page 3 of that statement. Do you have the English one in front of you or the Croatian one?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatian one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you find the paragraph that begins "on the 13th of December, four colleagues from the town planning office..."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it read -- can you just read what that paragraph says, please.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 13th of December, four colleagues from the town planning office (Anka Buzic, Zeljko Franetovic, Mirjana Karaman, and Davorka Kunic) and I attended at the institute and made ourselves available to assist in the investigations, which by this time were well underway."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you told the investigator when you spoke to him in July 2000?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consult any notes, records, or diaries when you gave him that date?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not consult them. And this date was just an approximation which I had in my memory at the time. So the 13th, when I said the 13th, we can assume that it was on or about the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having looked at the records which are in Exhibit P174, can you say now whether the date of the 13th of December in your statement is correct or incorrect? Sorry, P174, for your information, is the extract of all the buildings you inspected, including the date -- which, of course, include the date of inspection.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note that the 10th of December was mentioned as the date when I went out on inspection which confirms my prior statement that it was on or about the 13th. In this case, it was even earlier, possibly on the 10th, and everything confirms that. I did not have the material at the time when I provided the statement. It was all based on my recollection. And, as I can see, I didn't go too far wrong in what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to show you another video. It's Exhibit P145, which was tendered during the evidence of Admiral Jokic. The description which has been given of this video is one taken by some Croatian people who were basically following around a commission from the JNA as it was videoing parts of the Old Town on the 8th of December 1991. Just to confirm, you've seen -- have you seen a copy of this 20-minute video in Dubrovnik and in the offices of the OTP over the last few days?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this footage, I cannot tell whether it's something that I have seen before or not. So could you please show me a little bit of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll start right at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you that again later, if necessary. Stopping at 0.08, can you identify that building and the roof which has a tarpaulin over it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Sponza. It's close to the bell tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop. At time of 21 seconds, can you identify that building.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the St. Blaise church terrace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see any signs of recent damage on that -- that particular shot? We'll just take it back a second.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What do you mean by "recent damage"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Damage which had occurred around the time the video was taken.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of December, the shelling occurred and the damage probably also occurred on the 6th of December, if this is what you're talking about. Then in that context, yes, then, it is a recent hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a close-up shot -- 25 seconds. What does that show? It shows something just above a balcony rail.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the wall. It's a stone relief that was damaged. I remember that detail very well. That is all that I can tell you about that. It was probably caused by a direct or indirect shell hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop you there. It shows some steps. That's at the time of 38. Which steps are those?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the same church, but this is the side from the Gradska Kavana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom stair, there seems to be some damage to that. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was most probably damaged by shrapnel coming from impact in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop you there at 51 to 53. Was that another shot of St. Vlaho's church, taken from the top of the church looking down?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's the same terrace balustrade. And also, this is the same part of the stone relief and the pillar of the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stopped at a time of 56. Is that what you're referring to, the stone relief and the pillar of the church?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a little bit more to the right, just above the pointer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to comment upon the three holes which appear to be in a stone pillar which is in the middle of the still. Time of 56.4.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are shrapnel traces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go back. Between 57 and one -- 57 seconds and 1.04, there was a hole in the pavement of something. Where is that? Sorry, it was 58.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are traces of a direct hit or direct impact by a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this shot, this frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, just where the hole was.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to have a broader view of it. I think it's Luza. I think it's in front -- yeah, yeah, that's it. It's the square in front of Sponza, St. Blaise's, and the bell tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1.16, it's focussing on some rooftops which is on the Stradun. Can you identify which building that is or where that is on the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, this is a building that belongs to the second row of houses on Stradun. I would need to have a broader view now in order to be able to assess where it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 1.20, there's a shot looking up a street with a pile of rubble and debris up to the left. Which street is that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is one of the streets going from Stradun to Prijeko. I assume this is Boskoviceva, but if you could show me a bit more perhaps I could confirm that it really is Boskoviceva. Yes, it is Boskoviceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stopping at 1.35, could you recognise where those buildings were?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have 1.37 here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is Boskoviceva Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've stopped at 1.38, and there's a pillar with a gutter to the right. What can you say about where that building is and what it shows?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the beginning of Boskoviceva Street, so it's part of Stradun. These are traces of the vaults that existed before the great earthquake in Dubrovnik, the earthquake of 1667. So this detail belongs to the building we discussed just now, Boskoviceva Street at the very beginning by Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about damage? Can you see any damage to any structure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The damage can be seen. The broken stone, the profiles that were damaged. It is possible that this came from shrapnel. So indirect impact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1.44, we'll stop there. Do you recognise that street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the next street going towards the Franciscan cloister. It's Dropceva. Also, this is the beginning of the street at Stradun leading towards Prijeko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a person doing something with some tiles there at 1.50. What can you see in this shot in relation to building debris and rubble and materials?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said a few minutes ago. The roof material was falling into the street all smashed. So these were small pieces or big pieces. This shows the situation when these roof tiles were being removed already with the hope of having them repaired and having the roofs repaired. So that is what I consider to be noteworthy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that was Dropceva Street the next one up from Boskovica. Is that from Stradun going towards Prijeko?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop there. That's at 2.09. Where is that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to rewind it so that I can see the wider context. Stop. So, I can recognise this. In the upper right-hand corner of this still, we can see the beginning of Dropceva Street, and this closed area is the ground floor of the house that actually belongs to Dropceva Street. So this shot was taken from Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described shrapnel --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Dropceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described shrapnel damage to buildings you saw on the video P66 to buildings on Stradun. Can you see any shrapnel damage to those particular buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite evident. We called this piketine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning what?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's these tiny little shards of -- coming from the stone walls, and this was caused by the metal parts of the shells that fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would buildings -- were other buildings on the Stradun in this state after the 6th of December? That's the building which is at-- time at 2.08.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, and that goes for the majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about before the 6th of December? You told the Trial Chamber yesterday you were regularly visiting your mother once or twice a week before the 6th of December. Were the buildings along the Stradun in that condition before the 6th of December? When I say "condition," I mean bearing those types of shrapnel marks?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were some in part. I cannot remember the exact localities, but there were some before the 6th, too. Again, I say it cannot be compared to the period after the 6th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Time of 2.24. Can you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is a building in Stradun facing the north in relation to the position of Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean facing towards Srdj. Is that what you mean by facing towards the north?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see any damage to that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see damage in the upper right-hand corner. I can see the cornice, and also I can see the window that is damaged, the wooden shutter was broken. And there's even more damage than that that can be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2.37, there's a video still of a building. Where is that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a building in Stradun which belongs to a particular row of buildings that are on the northern side of Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are the cross streets?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see from this particular still. If you could give me a broader view, perhaps I could say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that assist?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that this is either Kuniceva or another street like that viewed in respect of the bell tower of the Franciscan cloister and recognising the building that we can see right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2.54 shows the pavement. Is there a hole at about 2.54? Is that also on the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have before me 02.56, but I did see the previous footage, and that is a hole in the pavement on the Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that hole, or a hole similar to that, on the Stradun before the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If it had been there before, it would have been cleared up, at least to a certain extent and it wouldn't have been in this condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want you to comment about 2.55, 56, after that hole you can see some red -- stop -- red material on the pavement around the channel that runs through the middle of Stradun. What is that red material?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The recording is not clear enough, but I think that I can say that these are smashed-up roof tiles that fell from the roof onto the pavement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just whereabouts on Stradun is the shot at 2.56?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was recorded before Siroka. So practically it is the block with which Siroka begins, or rather ends -- or rather Stradun and Siroka Ulica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 3.11, there are two windows and doors. Do you recognise those buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
